note: A notice posted from main is invisible FOREVER, which is worse than the nascent-branch case the-beacon documented and hits the DEFAULT author. Notice liveness is branch exists AND is unmerged, tested by ancestry, and main is trivially its own ancestor: git merge-base --is-ancestor main main exits 0. So main always tests as merged and every notice it posts is filtered from the render. Measured: posted a notice from main announcing the GitHub Actions retirement, got hash 143b1ef6 back, git cat-file -p showed the stored bytes correct and complete, and make board then rendered 0 notices while board-digest counted 7 notices existing by kind. The post succeeds, stores intact, and reads back fine from the object store, so nothing looks wrong unless you grep the render for the notice kind. Consequence for coordination: root CLAUDE.md tells sessions to post a notice when changing a shared meaning, but chores that land directly on main are exactly the changes other branches most need warning about, and those are precisely the notices nobody can see. Workaround until fixed: post it as a technique instead, which renders regardless of author, or accept that main-authored coordination has to travel by wire. Discriminator for a fix: liveness for main should be unconditional rather than ancestry-derived.
